processing: Little is documented for this cultivar alone. As with other Japanese black teas, leaf is withered, rolled, oxidised and dried.
harvest_season: Not well recorded for this cultivar. Japanese black teas are commonly picked in spring and summer.
appearance_dry: Typical of Japanese black tea, dark brown twisted leaf.
appearance_liquor: Typical of Japanese black tea, a clear amber-red.
appearance_wet: Typical of Japanese black tea, soft copper-brown leaf.
taste_profile: No reliable tasting description exists for this cultivar on its own; Japanese black teas are typically light on astringency with a soft sweetness.

brewing.notes: A general starting point for Japanese black tea. Lengthen the second steep slightly.

vintage_note: As is usual for Japanese black tea, it would be sold in small lots by harvest year with the grower named. Fresher lots hold their aroma better, so aim for the current or previous year.
description:
Benikaori is a Japanese cultivar listed for black tea. The name reads as crimson plus fragrance, though that is only what the words mean, not a tasting note. Little else is documented about it.

As with other Japanese black teas, processing follows the usual path of withering, rolling, oxidation and drying.

Expect the class's soft sweetness and low astringency rather than anything brisk, and brew it just under the boil. If you find a lot, ask the grower about the picking season.
history: Little is documented about where and when Benikaori was bred, who released it, or how widely it is planted.
